thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: prefix cache miss spike detected on prod-app (p50 latency up 80%) — paging eng-sre oncall @sarah.nguyen at 1865004321

sarah.nguyen: saw the alert, joining. any customer-facing errors? :eyes:

ops-bot: impact summary: 03:10-03:28 UTC: ~12% of requests returned degraded responses (timed fallback to model_v1_small). Top impacted routes: /generate, /chat. No 5xxs, higher latency & increased cost due to fallback.

james.patel: I'm on phone but looking at dashboards. prefix_kv_hitrate dropped from 92% -> 38% around 03:09 UTC.

ria.kim: copying key graphs to the thread: (links) https://grafana.redwood/prod/prefix_kv/hitrate, https://logs.redwood/s/abcd1234?from=1865004000

sarah.nguyen: good, quick hypotheses: (1) accidental TTL/eviction change (2) cache invalidation job ran (3) upstream client changed keys/prefix format. Let's gather logs + who deployed around 03:05-03:10.

james.patel: checking deploys: deploy-bot shows a config push at 03:06 by ria.kim — `kv_ttl_seconds=60` -> `kv_ttl_seconds=0` in staging config. Noted.

ria.kim: that was a staging tweak for a test; I thought it was scoped to staging. checking repo... oh crap, the prom config flip accidentally applied to prod via templating bug.

sarah.nguyen: ok that would explain mass expiration. mitigation path: revert config -> warm prefix caches or increase TTL -> enable fallback routing to dedicated cache tier. Which is fastest?

james.patel: fastest is revert config and run targeted warm for hot prefixes. Revert already queued: `kubectl set env deploy/cache-config KV_TTL_SECONDS=3600 -n prod` — executing now.

ops-bot: runbook step triggered: manual-warm for top-100 prefixes (script: `scripts/warm_prefixes.sh --list hot_prefixes_24h.txt --parallel 16`).

ria.kim: running warm script now on a deduped list. I'll post logs here.

sarah.nguyen: sending a quick customer impact note to SRE-Support to prepare incident page. We need timeline + affected customers. @james, can you pull top customers by request rate from 03:08-03:20?

james.patel: pulling now. top impacted tenants: beta-acme (10% errors), appwise (7%), internal-dev (4%). Preparing CSV.

ria.kim: warm script output (tail):
```
[03:14:22] warming prefix: `user/ua/` -> 120/120 OK
[03:14:22] warming prefix: `session/global/` -> 8/120 OK
[03:14:23] warming prefix: `org/` -> 0/120 MISS (deprecated key format?)
[03:15:01] warmed 84/100 prefixes, 16 failed (rate-limited)
```

sarah.nguyen: interesting that `org/` returns 0 — could be mismatched key encoding after template change. James, check client header changes.

james.patel: client headers unchanged. However, at 03:06 we saw an ingress rewrite rule change in the templating service that strips trailing slashes — might change prefix keys. Correlating...

eng-sre-oncall: joining thread. From infra: cache eviction spike logs show mass TTL expirations at 03:07:12 across 5k shards. Policy: if TTL == 0 => immediate eviction.

ria.kim: confirmed I accidentally set `KV_TTL_SECONDS=0` for a prod template group. Also the templating rollout was simultaneous across regions at 03:06:45, which matches drop. I rolled back the template at 03:16:40.

incident-bot: AUTO: rollback detected by deploy-bot at 03:16:40 (deploy id: dpl_2026_03_15_031640). Observed metrics: prefix_kv_hitrate recovering to 70% by 03:22.

sarah.nguyen: mitigation summary so far: (a) rollback at 03:16:40 (b) warm job started 03:14 and completed with partial success 03:18 (c) manual fallback to model_v1_small remained active until 03:24.

james.patel: hitrate curve: 92% -> 38% at 03:09 -> rollback at 03:16 -> 70% at 03:22 -> 88% at 03:28. Latency returned to normal by 03:30.

ria.kim: creating an initial timeline doc in /incidents/1865004321/notes.md. Uploading logs bundle to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1865004321/logs.tar.gz

sarah.nguyen: customer comms: product-impacting, but no data loss, degraded quality/timeouts to fallback model. Recommend outreach to top tenants: beta-acme and appwise. Assign @james to draft?

james.patel: I'll draft now. Quick note in draft: root cause was templating error applying staging change to prod which set KV_TTL_SECONDS=0 causing mass invalidation.

eng-sre-oncall: additional note: caching layer did not persist a hot-key replication to secondary tier for ~240s due to a bug in repaint queue under high eviction pressure. That slowed warm success. Creating ticket INFRA-4523.

sarah.nguyen: OK, action items: 1) RCA doc + timeline (owner: ria.kim) 2) Fix templating guard to prevent zero-ttl -> rollout policy + opt-out (owner: ria.kim) 3) Improve warm script backoff and replication (owner: eng-sre) 4) Customer outreach (owner: james.patel) 5) Postmortem review w/ product (owner: sarah.nguyen).

ria.kim: will own the RCA and templating guard. Estimated ETA for RCA draft: EOD today. Adding notes: reproduce steps, logs, diff of template change, warm script output, affected tenant list.

james.patel: drafted customer note and shared in #customer-comms. Asking for review.

ops-bot: incident severity updated to Sev3 at 03:30 after mitigation.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: oncall rotation change in 20m. @sarah.nguyen to handoff to @eng-sre-oncall with notes.

sarah.nguyen: handing off now. key facts in handoff: root cause templating zero-ttl, rollback at 03:16, partial warm completed, replication lag issue INFRA-4523, customer list attached.

eng-sre-oncall: taking over. I'll own the post-incident follow-ups and ensure the templating guard patch lands in next deploy window. Also will add a canary check to templating service to detect dangerous TTL values.

ria.kim: appended a repro snippet to RCA draft:
```
# repro
kubectl apply -f templates/prod/cache-config.yaml --namespace=prod
# check env
kubectl get deploy cache-config -n prod -o yaml | grep KV_TTL_SECONDS
```

sarah.nguyen: final note for timeline: root cause timestamp: 03:06:45 (templating rollout), detection: 03:09 (alerts), mitigation start: 03:14 (warm), rollback: 03:16:40, recovery to baseline: 03:28-03:30.

eng-sre-oncall: creating follow-up epic: EPI-7782 (templating guards + warm robustness). Linking INFRA-4523 and the RCA doc.

james.patel: customer comms sent to beta-acme and appwise. They asked for a short summary and whether any data was lost. I indicated no data loss and provided timeline + mitigation steps.

ria.kim: thanks everyone. I'll publish the RCA draft by EOD and assign PRs for the guard + template tests.

sarah.nguyen: great job triaging quickly. We'll do a blameless postmortem on Monday. If anyone has further logs or notes, drop them in the RCA doc. :raised_hands:

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (auto) at 03:40 UTC — severity downgraded to monitor. Thread archived for RCA drafting.
